title: [AMD] Add Radix-4 MoE top-k router kernel for Kimi-K3 routing (#34490)
body:
co-author: @kkHuang-amd 

## Motivation


Kimi-K3 routes 16 of 896 experts, ungrouped. That lands on aiter's generic `biased_grouped_topk`, which spends one round per selected expert — cost tracks `topk`, ~10.4us per layer on MI355X. aiter's faster pivot-based path is gated on DeepSeek's exact shape (256 experts, 8 groups, top-8), so K3 never reaches it.

Set `SGLANG_K3_RADIX4_TOPK=1` to enable the radix4 topk path.

## Modifications


Radix-4 select for this shape: the pivot is resolved four key bits at a time, so the round count follows the key width rather than `topk`. Tuned to CDNA — a 16-bin histogram packed as nibbles into one 64-bit register, experts spread over several waves, and a 4-step DPP prefix sum plus a ballot in place of the 16-step walk over the bins.
- `kernels/jit/csrc/moe/route_radix4_hip.cuh` — kernel (CDNA-only; uses amdgcn DPP and wave64 ballots)
- `kernels/ops/moe/moe_route_radix4.py` — JIT wrapper
- `srt/layers/moe/topk.py` — dispatch for covered inputs 
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_route_radix4.py` — pinned against real aiter (oracle match, tie order, NaN/extremes/saturated rows, reproducibility, graph replay, coverage gating)


`covered()` is narrow: `[M, 896]` row-contiguous scores, top-16, ungrouped, and `M <= 1024`. Everything else stays on aiter. The token cap is a performance gate rather than a correctness one — the kernel runs one block per token, so past ~1.5k tokens the grid saturates the machine and spreading a token over four waves costs more than it buys. Decode batches sit well under the cap; prefill chunks are far above it and stay on aiter.

### tie contract
When scores tie exactly, the common approach (the CUDA router in route_radix.cuh) breaks the tie by expert id -- whichever id is smaller wins. aiter's biased_grouped_topk instead resolves ties via an order implicit in its internal wave64 max reduction (warp reduction), which depends on how it pairwise-compares threads at the hardware level and has no direct relation to expert id.

We currently dispatch by M (batch size): large-M prefill goes to aiter's topk implementation, small-M decode goes to this radix4 topk implementation we wrote ourselves. If the two implementations pick different experts on a tie, the same token would get routed to different experts purely because it showed up during prefill versus decode -- prefill and decode routing would disagree.

So our current approach is to have our own kernel replicate aiter's tie-break order. kAiterTieLaneRank (in route_radix4_hip.cuh) is that order, read off directly b …[truncated]

title: [Weight Cache] Support static DP/EP layouts (#33684)
body:
## Motivation

Weight-cache daemons and engines must construct identical model-parallel layouts before CUDA IPC can safely map a cached MoE shard. The existing daemon launcher rejected `dp_size > 1`, preventing static DP/EP deployments from using the daemon-backed weight cache.

This change adds static DP/EP layout support to the CUDA IPC weight-cache path. It is the implementation foundation for the DP/EP roadmap in #33522.

## Modifications

- Propagate static DP/EP, MoE DP, attention DP, MoE A2A, and DeepEP-mode configuration from the engine into weight-cache daemons.
- Initialize daemon-side model-parallel and MoE state with the same static layout as the engine.
- Extend `CacheConfig` with MoE DP/EP shard identity and layout fields, so daemon/client compatibility validation rejects incompatible shards.
- Fix static Mooncake EP dispatch to use an all-active rank mask when Elastic EP state is absent.
- Route Qwen3 MoE through the existing DeepEP-class backend predicate so Mooncake uses the EP execution path.
- Add CPU coverage for MoE shard-rank calculation, extended cache fingerprints, and daemon DeepEP-mode forwarding.

The implementation supports static layouts. Dynamic expert placement, EPLB, redundant experts, and recovery lifecycle ownership remain roadmap work.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [AMD][Fix] Route MoRI through the Qwen MoE all-to-all path (#32039)
body:
## Motivation

Serving **Qwen3.5 MoE** (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4) with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` on MI355X/ROCm (DP=1 / TP=2, EP=2) produced near-zero accuracy — gsm8k **0.006**.

The Qwen2/Qwen3 MoE gates key on `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()`, which recognises **only** pure DeepEP. MoRI is a DeepEP-class backend and needs the same per-rank EP expert layout, so under MoRI the block silently fell through to the plain-TP path:

- the shared expert stayed sharded by TP=2, so each token computed only one shared-expert shard and lost the other half of the contribution;
- `can_fuse_shared_expert` still allowed the fusion, placing the shared expert in a **global** slot that the per-rank EP layers never allocate;
- the block never entered `_forward_deepep()`, so the routed experts never went through the MoRI dispatch/combine at all.

The corrupted first token then poisons everything generated after it.

This PR is the correctness follow-up to #31793 (which only disabled the global-slot shared-expert fusion to get MoRI past the init crash).

## Modifications

Add `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()` alongside the existing `is_deepep()` at the four gates in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`: `can_fuse_shared_expert` (`:153`), the shared-expert TP override (`:328`), the EP layout branch (`:347`), and the forward dispatch (`:563`).

MoRI now uses the correct per-rank EP expert layout, replicates the shared expert per rank (`tp_rank=0, tp_size=1`), enters `_forward_deepep()`, and each token receives the full shared-expert output.

The remaining DeepEP-class backends (Mooncake, PPLX) are deliberately **not** included — they have no Qwen MoE coverage to validate against, so `is_mori()` keeps the change byte-identical to `main` for the CUDA-side backends this PR does not exercise.

A CPU unit test in `test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` pins that `can_fuse_shared_expert` refuses for both `deepep` and `mori`, and still fuses on plain TP.

## Two earlier changes have been removed from this PR

On-hardware re-validation no longer shows either of the two bugs they targeted.

MoRI normal mode **is** CUDA-graph safe, as @Duyi-Wang said. `mori_cpp.build_args` returns an args struct whose values (input/indices pointers, `curRankNumToken`, and the preallocated shmem buffer pointers) are snapshotted per graph node by `hipModuleLaunchKernel`, and every comm buffer has fixed capacity and a stable address.

title: [MoE] Gather the cutlass MoE activation and its scales in one launch (#34915)
body: ## Motivation The fp8 blockwise CUTLASS MoE quantizes its activation once and then replicates rows per routed expert, so the gather it performs walks a `dst2src` map of `m * topk` entries. Until now it walked that map twice: one `shuffle_rows` launch for the fp8 values and a second one for the fp32 group scales. The second walk moves a thirty-second of the bytes the first one does — `k // 128` fp32 against `k` fp8 — so as a launch of its own it is almost entirely latency. That is exactly the cost that matters where this path spends its time: at low concurrency the whole gather is a few tens of KB, and the launch is the work. Where the gather sits, between quantizing the activation once and the first grouped GEMM: ## Modifications A triton kernel that walks the map once and writes both tensors, registered as a TRITON `KernelSpec` (`op="moe.shuffle_rows_with_scales"`) per RFC #29630. The grid is `(dst_row, k_tile)`; the tile that owns column 0 also carries that row's scales, which are 1/32 the width and do not deserve a launch of their own. The non-mxfp8 path calls it instead of the two `shuffle_rows`. The SM100 mxfp8 ES branch gathers a bf16 activation through a different kernel and is untouched. The two blue arrows are the point: `token 0` is read twice because it routes to two experts, which is why the gather moves `topk` times the rows the quantizer ever saw. The narrow cell trailing each row is that row's scales, and it travels under the same `a_map` — that shared map is the whole reason one kernel can produce both. Rows are copied as bytes rather than as fp8 — the values are never decoded — so the kernel works for any 1-byte dtype and cannot perturb them. Row bases are computed in int64, matching the CUDA `shuffle_rows` it replaces, since `rows * k` overflows int32 well inside the shapes this path serves. The kernel also masks its tails. The CUDA `shuffle_rows` takes its element count as `num_cols / elems_per_thread` with no remainder handling, so it only moves a whole fp32 scale row when `(k // 128) % 4 == 0`; every `k` that is a multiple of 512 is unaffected either way, which covers the shapes this path serves today. **mxfp8 MoE is not affected by this PR.** It will be addressed in the next PR. ## Accuracy Tests The result is **bit-identical** t …[truncated]

title: [MegaMoE] Respect padded MXFP8 scale row strides in pre-dispatch (#36237)
body:
Replaces #36007. This branch was rebuilt directly on the latest required `main` commit (`1ec20fd`) because the prior branch was blocked by the CI rebase gate.

## Summary

Update `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` to honor the physical row stride of DeepGEMM's MXFP8 scale output instead of assuming packed rows.

DeepGEMM stores one scale byte per 32 hidden elements and aligns each token row to 16 bytes for TMA:

    logical row bytes  = H / 32
    physical row bytes = align_up(H / 32, 16)

Under DeepGEMM's `H % 128 == 0` layout requirement, padding is needed whenever `H % 512 != 0`:

| H | Logical row | Physical row | Padding |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2176 | 68 B | 80 B | 12 B |
| 2304 | 72 B | 80 B | 8 B |
| 2432 | 76 B | 80 B | 4 B |
| 2560 | 80 B | 80 B | 0 B |

Packed addressing misplaces scale rows after token 0. Once DeepGEMM exposes the correct physical stride, the existing contiguous-tensor check rejects the view instead.

Accept padded row-major scale views, validate their logical width and alignment, and use `buf_x_sf.stride(0)` when addressing each token row. Already-aligned layouts are unchanged.

## Modifications

- Accept row-major scale views with a contiguous inner dimension and a padded outer stride.
- Pass the physical row stride in bytes to the CUDA kernel and use it for each token's scale row.
- Validate the logical row width and the 16-byte alignment required by the DeepGEMM buffer.
- Add a Blackwell regression test that verifies logical scale bytes are written while row padding and unused rows remain unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Ran the focused regression test on an NVIDIA GB300, applying the test to both revisions:

```text

this PR:                 1 passed in 14.44s
```


title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 destination offset overflow in CUTLASS MoE pre-reorder (#35188)
body: ## Motivation `pre_reorder_triton_kernel_for_cutlass_moe` loads `dst_idx` from the `src2dst` mapping as an `int32` and uses it to calculate the destination address: ```python dst_ptr_offs + dst_idx * hidden_size ``` Because `dst_idx` is 32-bit, `dst_idx * hidden_size` can overflow signed 32-bit arithmetic when the destination activation buffer contains more than `2**31` elements. For example, with `hidden_size = 6144`, the first overflowing destination row is: ```text ceil(2**31 / 6144) = 349,526 ``` This is reachable during large expert-parallel prefill workloads. The wrapped offset can cause a CUDA illegal memory access or write to an incorrect GPU address. ## Modifications Promote `dst_idx` to `tl.int64` immediately after loading it: ```python dst_idx = tl.load(token_src2dst_ptr + idx).to(tl.int64) ``` This ensures that the multiplication by `hidden_size` and the destination pointer offset are evaluated using 64-bit arithmetic. The `src2dst` mapping remains `int32`; only the address calculation is widened. ## Accuracy Tests The change only affects destination address arithmetic. Outputs below the signed 32-bit offset boundary remain unchanged. The overflow boundary can be validated with an FP8 destination buffer using: - `hidden_size = 6144` - `dst_idx = 349,526` - A destination element offset greater than `2**31` - One BF16 input row converted and written to the selected FP8 row Expected behavior: - Before the fix: CUDA illegal memory access or an incorrect destination write. - After the fix: the selected destination row matches the FP8-converted input row. Large-offset validation requires a CUDA GPU with enough memory for a contiguous allocation larger than 2 GiB. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The change adds one scalar `int32`-to-`int64` conversion for each valid routed destination. It does not change the number of loads, stores, kernel launches, or transferred elements. ## Checklist --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32833006827](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32833006827) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32833007031](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32833007031) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #32833006686](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32833006686)

# [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3

## Summary

This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined.

Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses:

- an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access;
- direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers;
- asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and
- a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts.

The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path.

## Supported Scope

`ExpertPackModelLoader` is selected only with `--load-format expert_pack`. Official checkpoints loaded through the standard `auto` or `safetensors` paths never enter this loader.

The currently validated DeepSeek input is the single-file MXFP4 GGUF used by `frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`. Its routed expert matrices use `MXFP4`; the large non-routed matrices are mostly `Q8_0`, router input weights are `BF16`, and the inventory also contains `F32` and `I32` normalization or auxiliary tensors. The inspected GGUF contains 129 `MXFP4`, 512 `Q8_0`, 43 `BF16`, 641 `F32`, and 3 `I32` tensors. It contains no FP8 tensors.

The other validated input is the text-only 38-shard `KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf`, whose routed experts use Q2_K for gate/up and Q3_K for down. The Kimi launcher extracts the official `text_config` into a flat `KimiLinearConfig`; the complete multimodal Kimi-K3 checkpoint is not supported by this loader. Other GGUF quantization variants have not been validated and are not currently claimed as supported.

```bash
python3 -m pip install -e "python"
```

```bash
title: Fix OOB read in mxfp4 MoE weight scales on Hopper (#36456)
body:
## Motivation

`test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4.py` is intermittently red on `4-gpu-h100`. It is not an
accuracy failure -- the server dies mid-eval and every request returns empty, so the
score is exactly `0.0`:

```
coredump: Detected an exception of type CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (14)
coredump:   #0  _matmul_NNT_bf16xbf16xmxfp4_32x256x128x1_swiglu   (_matmul.py:371)
AssertionError: 0.0 not greater than or equal to 0.58
```

## Root cause

`triton_kernels` hard-forces `block_k=128` for mxfp4 on Hopper
(`opt_flags_nvidia.compute_block_k`), and its `HOPPER_SCALE` branch loads the weight
scales **unmasked** -- `_matmul.py:371`, versus the masked STRIDED path at `:375`.
`mask_k_scale` is only computed for STRIDED, so the scale K axis is unguarded.

The kernel walks that axis for `cdiv(K, 128)` full 128-wide tiles, so any K that is not
a multiple of 128 reads past the tensor. For gpt-oss (`K = hidden_size = 2880`):

```
k_tiles = cdiv(2880, 128) = 23  ->  walks 23 * 128 = 2944
swizzled row = (2880/32) * 32   =            2880     (SWIZZLE_ALIGN_K is only 2)
                                             ----
                                   64 rows of overread
```

Because the kernel indexes `WMxScale + expt_id * stride_w_mx_e`, the overread only
leaves the allocation for the **last expert** (3,072 B past the end of the 17.7 MB
tensor); for experts 0-126 it lands in the next expert's slab, where the matching `w`
values are already masked to zero. Only the `swiglu`/gate_up matmul is affected --
`w2`'s K is the padded intermediate (768), a multiple of 128.

**Why it is intermittent:** the read happens on every gpt-oss mxfp4 forward on Hopper;
whether it *faults* depends on whether the following page is mapped, which shifts with
allocator layout. It also needs expert 127 actually routed, which is why the small
warmup passes and the 198-request eval burst dies.

Not a recent regression: `hidden_size` has never been padded in the
`has_triton_kernels` branch, and the `block_k=128` forcing is upstream.

## Fix

Pad the scale K extent (90 -> 92, giving a 2944 B row) up to the kernel's walk, in
`_swizzle_mxfp4` after weight loading -- so the weight loader, `create_weights` shapes
and activation padding are all untouched. `block_k` stays 128.

The padding is numerically inert: the matching `w` values are masked to zero by the
kernel and `_UE8M0_ONE` (127) is the neutral E8M0 scale. No-op for `w2`. Costs +14 MB
per GPU.

body:
> Reland of #29525, reverted by #35568 because its e2e test used an
> unregistered CI runner name. This reland restores the backend and fixes that
> registration without changing unrelated CI configuration.

## Motivation

Add DeepEP v2 `ElasticBuffer` as a standalone MoE A2A backend named
`deepep_v2`, alongside the existing `deepep` backend. Its fixed-capacity
communication shapes make decode CUDA-graph capturable with both single-node
and multi-node topologies.

## Supported scope

| Area | Supported in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Models | `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` |
| Expert precision | Dynamic blockwise FP8, 128x128 weight blocks |
| MoE runner | `deep_gemm` |
| Backend modes | `--deepep-v2-mode direct|hybrid` |
| DeepEP package | `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.2` (`deep_ep 2.1.0`) |

`direct` and `hybrid` select the ElasticBuffer topology; they are not aliases
for legacy DeepEP `low_latency` and `normal`. Decode uses the expanded masked
layout, while extend/prefill uses the contiguous layout in either mode.

This intentionally does not claim support for other MoE architectures or
quantization contracts. In particular, Qwen3.8
(`Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), BF16 experts, MXFP8, non-DeepGEMM runners,
deterministic inference, and a speculative draft worker using `deepep_v2` are
not supported by this landing. These configurations now fail before A2A
execution instead of reaching a model-specific forward path with incorrect
post-expert reduction or incompatible activation scales.

- Adds an independent `DeepEPv2Dispatcher` using ElasticBuffer dispatch and

- Stores ElasticBuffer state in `RuntimeContext` resources so context reset and

title: [AMD] Enable moe_a2a_backend=mori for DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism (#35611)
body:
Enables DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism to use Mori for MoE all-to-all.

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism rejected `moe_a2a_backend=mori`, although Mori already uses the same rank-local EP dispatch/combine path as DeepEP.

## Changes

- Add `mori` to the DeepSeek-V4 CP validation whitelist.
- Add `is_mori()` to the matching model-side backend gate.

No dispatcher, collective, or compute kernel is changed.

## Why this is safe

DeepSeek-V4 CP fixes `DP=1` and `CP=TP`; Mori resolution also fixes `EP=TP`. Each rank sends its local CP token shard through `forward_deepep`, and Mori combine returns complete outputs in source-rank order. The Mori path does not run the CP gather/reduce-scatter used by `a2a=none`, so its replicated shared expert is added once and is not affected by [#35535](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35535).

Short batches that cannot be CP-split fall back to replicated prefill, so Mori capacity must still cover `chunked_prefill_size`.

## Validation

On 8×MI355X with DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark, TP8/CP8, compared with matched non-CP Mori runs:

- Short sweep: `40/40` stable first-token matches, mean top-1 logprob delta `-0.015`.
- 4K–16K sweep: `14/14` deterministic lengths matched; one length was self-unstable and one hit the existing CP-v1 GPU fault.
- `pre-commit`, syntax checks, and a Mori CP validation smoke test pass.

CP+Mori TBO remains disabled. Generic Mori dynamic-capacity limits and the existing CP-v1 one-token-per-rank GPU fault are outside this PR.
```

title: [AMD][DSV4] perf: bound the MoRI receive buffer during decode (#36130)
body:
## Motivation

AITER sizes its quantization grid from the input row count
(`aiter/csrc/kernels/quant_kernels.cu`, `rows = input.numel() / cols`). Under
MoRI that input is the **padded** receive buffer
(`num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank * world_size` = 4096 * 8 = 32768 rows), not
the live tokens. `num_rows` is a device pointer used only for a per-block early
exit, so it cannot shrink the grid.

In decode the padding dominates: at concurrency 64 a rank carries at most 32
tokens, whose entire expert fan-in is 1792 rows, yet every kernel still launches
blocks covering 32768. The narrower the batch, the larger the share of that work
that is pure waste.

## Modification

Bound the row count at the worst case the receive buffer can actually see:
every rank routing a full decode graph's worth of tokens to this one,
`max_graph_tokens * world_size * topk`. `topk` already includes the fused shared
expert (`deepseek_v2.py` folds `num_fused_shared_experts` into `top_k`), so this
is a bound, not an estimate — at conc 64 it is `32 * 8 * 7 = 1792`, the exact
case where every rank sends every token-expert pair here.

The subtlety is *which* token count is safe to use. This code runs while a cuda
graph is **captured**, so the value is frozen into the graph and has to hold for
every later replay, including replays where a peer carries a wider batch than
the one seen at capture. Deriving it from the batch in hand would break as soon
as ranks replay different tiers — which they do in this configuration, since
neither `require_mlp_tp_gather()` nor `require_attn_tp_gather()` holds under
`--enable-dp-lm-head` with `--moe-dense-tp-size 1`.

So it is derived from the widest decode graph *any* rank will replay, taken from
`capture_bs` (already clamped by `req_to_token_pool.size`) and reduced with an
explicit `all_reduce(MAX)` at runner init, outside capture where a collective is
safe. `req_to_token_pool.size` is sized from measured free memory and so is not
guaranteed identical across ranks, hence a reduction rather than an assumption
of symmetry. A peer replaying a wider tier is then covered by construction, and
there is no synchronized-graph-tier requirement left to guard.

Two cases stay unbounded, because a bound below the real fan-in silently drops
rows from the all-to-all — wrong output rather than an error:

- **Prefill**, whose per-rank counts are uneven and not knowable here.
- **Anything outside capture.** Eager decode runs precisely when the batch
  exceeds every captured tier, so the published width would not bound it, and
  there is no graph to bake a saving into anyw …[truncated]

title: [AMD][DSV4] perf: MXFP8 MoRI dispatch to match the w4a8 MoE input format (#36119)
body:
## Motivation

DSv4's MoE runs `per_1x32` (MXFP4 weights), so AITER wants fp8 activations
carrying group-32 e8m0 microscales. None of MoRI's three shipped dispatch dtypes
produce that:

| dispatch | payload | scales | consequence |
| -------- | ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| bf16 | bf16 | none | receiver must quantize |
| fp8 | fp8 | group-128 fp32 | wrong group size -> fp8->bf16 upscale round trip |
| fp4 | fp4x2 | group-32 e8m0 | right scales, wrong payload -> `upscale_mxfp4` |

bf16 wins by default only because it is the one with no upscale kernel. But it
pushes the bf16->fp8 conversion to the **receive** side, and that is where the
cost is: AITER sizes its quant grid from the input row count
(`aiter/csrc/kernels/quant_kernels.cu`, `rows = input.numel() / cols`), and the
input is MoRI's *padded* receive buffer
(`num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank * world_size` = 3072 * 8 = 24576 rows) rather
than the ~112 live tokens decode actually carries. `num_rows` is a device
pointer used only for a per-block early exit, so it cannot shrink the grid.

DSR-1 never hits this: it is w8a8, its dispatch delivers fp8 with per-128 fp32
scales which is already the MoE's input format, so AITER takes the
`hidden_states.dtype == q_dtype_a` branch and runs no quant kernel at all.

## Modification

Adds an `mxfp8` dispatch mode that quantizes on the **send** side, over live
tokens, emitting the fp8 + group-32 e8m0 layout the MoE kernels consume
directly. Opt-in via `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=mxfp8`; the default stays
`bf16`, so existing deployments are untouched.

**Depends on the matching aiter change** (a8w4 mxfp8 passthrough in
`fused_moe.py`), which must land first.

title: fix(lora): build the MoE LoRA align JIT kernel on ROCm (#36379)
body:
## Problem

`moe_lora_align_block_size` is JIT-compiled, and the JIT build does not run hipify. On ROCm the kernel therefore fails to compile: `cub/cub.cuh` does not exist, `cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin` / `cudaFuncSetAttribute` / `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` have no HIP spellings in the JIT tree, and `hipFuncSetAttribute` takes a `const void *` rather than a function pointer.

MoE LoRA inference reaches this kernel from `_compute_lora_alignment`, so serving a MoE model with a LoRA adapter on ROCm aborts on the first such forward:

```
python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/lora/moe_lora_align_kernel.cu:9:10: fatal error: 'cub/cub.cuh' file not found
```

## Change

On ROCm, include hipCUB, alias `cub` to `hipcub`, and map the three attribute spellings to HIP — all local to `moe_lora_align_kernel.cu`. The kernel is passed as `const void *` through `std::bit_cast`, matching `setup_kernel_smem_once` in `deepseek_v4/topk_v1.cuh`. CUDA keeps CUB and the same call contract.

The aliases are deliberately *not* added to `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`. A JIT cache leaf is keyed on the content of its transitive dependency closure, and `utils.cuh` is in the closure of essentially every module (140 of the 190 JIT sources include it directly, the rest transitively via `tensor.h`). Editing it invalidates the whole cache. Measured on MI355X against a warm cache, appending a single comment to `utils.cuh` took three unrelated kernel tests from 5 s / 7 s / 5 s to 14 s / 89 s / 10 s; editing only `moe_lora_align_kernel.cu` left them at 5 s / 7 s / 5 s. That is what made an earlier revision of this PR time out `jit-kernel-unit-test` and `base-b-test-1-gpu-large` against the 30-minute step budget.

`test_moe_lora_align_block_size.py` is also registered for AMD CI. It was CUDA-only, so no job compiled this kernel on ROCm and the build break it fixes could not be caught.

## Validation

MI355X (`gfx950`), ROCm 7.2, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260826`:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_lora_align_block_size.py`: 32 passed from a cold JIT cache, in 27 s. The same suite is 32 failed on the base commit, on `cub/cub.cuh` not found.

title: [Blackwell] Reserve SMs for DeepGEMM MegaMoE grid barriers (#36657)
linked_issues: #30399 [Bug] PD disaggregation: GB200 Deepseek v4 Pro DeepGEMM grid sync timeout
body:
## Summary

- Reserve two SMs by default for Blackwell DeepGEMM MegaMoE launches.
- Scope the process-wide SM override to the actual MegaMoE kernel calls.
- Keep symmetric-buffer caching independent of the launch SM count.
- Keep Hopper/SM90 behavior unchanged and allow the reserve to be tuned or disabled.

## Root cause

Blackwell MegaMoE uses an even clustered grid with a whole-grid software barrier. If the launch uses every available SM while another CUDA stream temporarily occupies an SM, not all clusters can become resident. Resident clusters then wait at the barrier for clusters that cannot launch, eventually producing a DeepGEMM grid-sync timeout and a subsequent CUDA launch failure.

## Fix

For SM100 and newer, derive the MegaMoE launch size from DeepGEMM's current SM count and reserve two SMs by default. Round the active count down to an even number so it remains compatible with the two-CTA cluster.

Apply the override only around the DeepSeek and Kimi K3 `deep_gemm.fp8_fp4_mega_moe` calls, then restore DeepGEMM's process-wide setting even when launch setup raises. Gate computation, top-k selection, symmetric-buffer setup, and pre-dispatch continue to use the original setting. The symmetric-buffer cache key remains based only on parameters that affect buffer size or layout.

The separate SM90 MegaMoE implementation remains unchanged. This supersedes the closed #30592 with a smaller diff and explicit architecture gating.

Fixes #30399.

title: [Fix] Route the Mooncake MoE A2A backend through Kimi K3's EP-A2A / SP-MoE fast path (#36862)
body:
## Motivation

Kimi K3 selects two backend-specific optimizations at construction time:

- `self._ep_a2a` — when the MoE A2A backend routes each row to its experts directly, the MoE region consumes the rank-local rows (an SP-MoE token shard or the DP-local batch) with **no DP gather and no TP reduce**, and every global token is dispatched exactly once.
- `self._sp_moe` — on top of `_ep_a2a`, MoE layers with `attn_tp > 1` convert the deferred `o_proj` attention-TP all-reduce into a reduce-scatter, so the whole MoE front (norms, gate, latent projections, tp1 shared experts, A2A dispatch) runs on `1/attn_tp` of the rows and all-gathers back afterwards.

Both predicates already list the EP-A2A family — `is_megamoe()`, `is_deepep()`, `is_ascend_fuseep()`, `is_mori()` — but **Mooncake was missing**, even though `is_deepep_class_backend()` already classifies Mooncake as a DeepEP-family backend, `DeepEPMoE` documents that Mooncake shares the same interface, and the dispatcher factory builds the same `MaybeTboDeepEPDispatcher` with the `DEEPEP_LL` output format for both.

As a result, `moe_a2a_backend='mooncake'` correctly reached the Mooncake dispatcher on the data plane, but Kimi K3 still treated it as a plain TP/DP MoE:

| Backend  | `_ep_a2a` | `_sp_moe` |
| -------- | --------- | --------- |
| DeepEP   | True      | True      |
| Mooncake | False     | False     |

title: [Perf] Tune the W4AFP8 DeepEP low-latency requant launch geometry (#35760)
body:
## Motivation

`fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton()` turns DeepEP low-latency's per-token-group fp8
payload into the per-tensor fp8 that the first CUTLASS W4A8 grouped GEMM consumes. It is a pure
streaming pass — two bytes moved and two multiplies per element — but three properties of its
launch shape cost more than the arithmetic does.

**Access width.** A 1024-element tile over 8 warps is 4 B/thread, which is exactly where Triton
stops vectorizing: the compiled kernel contained only `ld.global.b32` / `st.global.b32` on every
part tested. 4 warps put 8 B/thread in flight and restore `v2.b32` accesses (2 warps reach
`v4.b32`, but measured slower than 4).

**Scale addressing.** Scales were indexed on the element axis
(`(k_offsets // 128) * stride2`), so each 1024-lane load resolved to 8 distinct addresses read
128 times each. The dispatcher returns the last two scale dims column-major for TMA
(`[E, M, hidden // 128]` with `stride1 == 1`), so those 8 addresses are `m` elements apart — a
scattered gather, replicated per row, per tile.

**Grid shape.** The m-grid was pinned to 32 programs per expert regardless of how many rows were
live, so at low-latency decode row counts most programs only loaded `masked_m`, compared, and
exited. This is by far the largest effect, and it grows with the local expert count: at 256 local
experts and one row each, the kernel spent 35 µs to move 3 µs of data.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/ep_moe_kernels.py`

- Tile the payload as `[G_BLOCK_SIZE, 128]` — whole scale groups — instead of a flat run of
  elements. The per-group scale becomes one scalar load, the fast axis stays contiguous, and a
  partial `k` masks whole groups. (`K_BLOCK_SIZE` is renamed `G_BLOCK_SIZE` because the constexpr
  changed units: it counted hidden elements, it now counts 128-wide scale groups, so 8 groups is
  the old 1024 elements.)
- Launch with 4 warps.
- A 1024-element tile per program, widening to 2048 once there are >= 32 local experts, where the
  expert axis alone fills the machine. The tile is kept in *elements* and divided by the scale
  group width to get `G_BLOCK_SIZE`, because bytes-per-thread is the tuned quantity -- a different
  group width would otherwise silently halve or double the measured tile. It is also rounded down
  to the payload, so a small hidden size never runs a mostly-masked tile.
- `requant_launch_geometry()` sizes the m-grid from `expected_rows`: one program per expected row,
  floored at 4, never above the historical 32, and additionally capped by the expert count while

title: [AMD] fix: do not emit a shared-expert marker twice on the per-rank slot path (#36515)
body:
## Motivation

On the per-rank fused shared-slot path the shared expert is appended after the
gate, by `fused_append_remap_shared_experts_deepep`. But `select_experts` also
passes `num_fused_shared_experts` down into the gate, so both of them emit a
shared marker.

Two things go wrong, neither of which raises:

**A routed expert is lost.** The gate is asked for
`K_routed = top_k - num_fused_shared_experts` slots and then spends one of them
on its own marker, so a top-6 routing silently becomes top-5.

**An id lands out of range.** The gate's marker is written at id `num_experts`,
and the DeepEP per-rank remap then shifts it one past the end of the expert
space — `384 -> 392` for 384 routed experts on EP8, where the valid ids are
`0..391`.

## Modification

Pass `0` to the gate when `has_per_rank_fused_shared_slots()` holds, so the
append is the single producer of the shared slot. Every other path keeps the
existing value, so this is a no-op off the per-rank shared-slot path.

14 lines in one file.

## Accuracy

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950), TP8 + DP8 attention + EP8/MoRI with
`--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`, which is the regime where the per-rank
shared-slot path is live. The arms differ only by this fix; each server asserts
which side it is on before measuring.

GSM8K, 1319 questions, parallel 1319:

| arm | accuracy | invalid |
| --- | -------- | ------- |
| without fix | 0.945 | 0.000 |
| with fix | 0.948 | 0.000 |

I would not read that gap as the effect. Four questions out of 1319 is inside
run-to-run noise for this benchmark, so the honest summary is that GSM8K cannot
resolve this bug either way — it is reported to show the fix does not regress,
not to claim it wins.

The case for the fix is the two defects themselves: a top-6 routing that is
actually running top-5, and an expert id written one past the end of the id
space. Both are silent, and neither is something a routing path should be doing
regardless of what an end-to-end score says.

title: [Bugfix] Accept int64 top-k IDs in FlashInfer routed MoE packer (#32882)
body:
[by Codex]

## Summary

- accept both `torch.int32` and `torch.int64` router IDs in `PackTopkIds`
- keep the existing in-kernel conversion to int32, avoiding a temporary cast allocation during CUDA-graph capture
- add focused coverage for both input dtypes, multiple shapes, exact reference parity, CUDA-graph capture/replay, and invalid input

This fixes a Qwen3 NVFP4 startup crash on Blackwell when torch compile uses the native top-k path:

```text
AssertionError: topk_ids must be int32, got torch.int64
```

## Regression history

This is a recent regression introduced by #25702.

Before #25702, `_pack_topk_for_flashinfer_routed` explicitly converted
`topk_ids` with `.to(torch.int32)`. The PR replaced that helper with
`PackTopkIds.execute`, whose Python wrapper asserted that IDs were already
int32. The Triton kernel itself has always converted loaded IDs with
`ids.to(tl.int32)`, so the wrapper rejected an input the kernel could process.

The strict packer originally came from #23882, where its initial caller supplied
int32 IDs. The incompatibility became a regression only when #25702 reused it
for the general FlashInfer routed-MoE paths.

## Before and after

Reproduced with `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` on NVIDIA B200
(`torch==2.11.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0):

Before:

```text
int32_eager=PASS
int64_eager=FAIL: AssertionError: topk_ids must be int32, got torch.int64
```

After:

```text
int32_eager=PASS
int64_eager=PASS
int64_cuda_graph=PASS
```

The patched output is bit-for-bit identical to `PackTopkIds.vanilla`.

## Why testing did not catch it

PR #25702 validated the routed MoE backend and reran the Blackwell model test,
but that test did not enable torch compile. The normal CUDA top-k implementation
returns int32 IDs, so it satisfied the new assertion.

With compile enabled for a batch-size-1 graph, `TopK.enter_torch_compile`
switches to `forward_native`; native `torch.topk` returns int64 indices. There
was no direct unit test defining `PackTopkIds`' accepted input dtypes, so this
contract mismatch escaped both the end-to-end and unit suites.

- Covered: routed FlashInfer MoE with the normal CUDA top-k path (int32)
- Missed: routed FlashInfer MoE + torch compile/native top-k (int64)
- Remediation in this PR: direct kernel-contract tests for int32 and int64,
  including int64 CUDA-graph capture/replay

## Validation

```text
python3 -m pytest -q test_pack_topk_ids.py
.........                                                                [100%]
9 passed in 14.55s
```

The focused reproducer also passed eager and CUDA-graph execution on B200.

title: [Kernel] Avoid zero-bias allocation in fused softmax routing (#36811)
body:
## Summary

Plain softmax routing has no correction bias, but `fused_topk` currently allocates and clears a device-side zero tensor on every call to satisfy the fused router kernel interface. This PR represents the same operation with a compile-time no-bias path, avoiding the allocation, fill, and bias load while preserving the existing sigmoid/correction-bias path.

## Changes

title: Fix native MoE handling of noncontiguous top-k IDs (#36407)

## Motivation

The native MoE path flattens `topk_ids` with `view`, which requires a stride-compatible tensor. Routing implementations may return valid noncontiguous top-k ID tensors, causing expert dispatch to fail even though the computation does not require contiguous storage.

## Modifications

- Replace `topk_ids.view(-1)` with `topk_ids.reshape(-1)` in the native MoE path.
- Preserve zero-copy behavior for stride-compatible layouts while materializing other layouts only when necessary.
- Add a CPU regression test comparing native MoE outputs for contiguous and strided top-k ID tensors.

## Accuracy Tests

A CPU regression test compares contiguous and noncontiguous representations of the same top-k IDs and verifies that they produce matching native MoE outputs.

**Motivation:** a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) box can hold DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but on

Following @Fridge003's review, the changes here that were not SM120 enablement now have
their own PRs:

- #35116 — allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode (correctness fix)
- #35118 — fuse the hc-prenorm combine into a Triton kernel (arch-independent)

**This PR now depends on #35116**: without it the page-split buffer is allocated under
inference mode during autotune and CUDA graph capture cannot write to it. Will rebase once
it lands.

The E2E tables below were measured with #35118 still in this tree. Measured separately on
the same box with only that kernel toggled (ISL 8K, BS1, TP4, deep_gemm MoE), it accounts
for **3.2% of the TPOT gain** (12.81 -> 12.40 ms, two repeats each, run-to-run spread

title: [XPU] Support GPT-OSS MXFP4 checkpoints on Intel XPU (#35751)
body:
## Enable GPT-OSS MXFP4 checkpoints on Intel XPU via the native W4A16 grouped GEMM

### Motivation

`openai/gpt-oss-20b` and `-120b` ship MXFP4-quantized MoE weights. Every SGLang MXFP4 kernel targets CUDA (`triton_kernels` / Marlin / FlashInfer cutlass), HIP (aiter) or CPU (AMX), so on `--device xpu` the checkpoint was rejected before any layer was built:

```
ValueError: Unknown quantization method: mxfp4. Must be one of ['fp8', 'mxfp8', ...]
  configs/model_config.py:_verify_quantization
```

This PR enables the checkpoint on XPU and serves it through the **sgl-kernel-xpu W4A16 grouped GEMM**: the packed MXFP4 weights are consumed **directly, at 4 bits, with no bf16 upcast**. Weights stay 4-bit in HBM and are dequantized per tile in registers inside the kernel — the whole point of MXFP4 on XPU.

> **Supersedes / consolidates #35742.** An earlier revision of this PR added a device-neutral *bf16-upcast* fallback (dequantize MXFP4 → bf16 at load, serve through the unquantized MoE). That path has been **removed**: it cost ~3.1× the weight memory and doesn't fit 120b. The native W4A16 routing from #35742 now lives here, so #35742 can be closed in favor of this PR.

### Modifications

Net **5 files, +117/-2** on top of upstream.

| # | Change | File | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Register `mxfp4` for XPU, gated on `is_xpu()` | `quantization/__init__.py` | Passes `_verify_quantization` on XPU so the checkpoint is accepted; backends with no MXFP4 kernel keep the existing clean error rather than silently upcasting. |
| 2 | Route MXFP4 MoE to the sgl-kernel-xpu W4A16 grouped GEMM: post-load is a free `.view(torch.int8)` of the packed nibbles, no upcast | `quantization/mxfp4.py` | The XPU grouped GEMM consumes the checkpoint layout (packed e2m1 `[E,N,K/2]` + N-outer ue8m0 g32 scales) directly. |
| 3 | Pad the per-rank MoE intermediate to a multiple of `mxfp4_block` (32) | `quantization/mxfp4.py` | See **Intermediate padding** below. |
| 4 | Forward the GPT-OSS swiglu config (`activation`, `gemm1_alpha`, `gemm1_clamp_limit`, `swiglu_limit`, `routed_scaling_factor`) that was previously dropped | `moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py` | Without it the experts silently computed a plain `silu*up` instead of the clamped `gate*sigmoid(gate*alpha)*(up+1)` the config asks for. |
| 5 | XPU quantization docs | `docs/…/quantization.mdx`, `docs/…/xpu.mdx` | Document the supported path. |

CUDA / HIP behaviour is unchanged: the generic post-load `else` is the upstream `triton_kernels.upcast_from_mxfp` fallback, and XPU never reaches it (it returns after the `.view(int8)`).
